title_ar: سماحة الشيخ  الددو  يحاضر في مركز البحوث والدراسات بالبنك الإسلامي للتنمية بجدة .
title_en: His Eminence Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures at the Research and Studies Centre of the Islamic Development Bank in Jeddah
body_ar:
سماحة الشيخ الددو يحاضر في مركز البحوث والدراسات بالبنك الإسلامي للتنمية بجدة .

ألقى سماحة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء محاضرة بمركز البحوث والدراسات بالبنك الإسلامي للتنمية بجدة اليوم الإثنين (15/ 09 / 1432 ه) الموافق (15/ 09 / 2011م ) تحت عنوان: أصول المعاملات في الشريعة الإسلامية وقد تناول فيها :

• طبيعة الشريعة في بيان الأحكام مقارنا بينها وبين القوانين الوضعية ، مبينا أن الشريعة تذكر الأحكام معللة ومسببة بينما تذكرها القوانين مجردة عن ذلك.

• النصوص القرآنية التي تناولت العقد والجوانب التي تناولتها منه .

• العقود المنهي وأوجه النهي عنها إجمالا.

• شروط العقود إجمالا .

• أوجه السعة والتضييق في العقود .

وقد ختمت المحاضرة بمناقشات من طرف الحضور حول جملة من القضايا أثارتها المحاضرة .

هذا وقد أدار المحاضرة الأستاذ الدكتور والخبير الإقتصادي العياشي فداد وحضرها جمع غفير من الباحثين في مركز الدراسات والبحوث بالبنك والمهتمين بالمعاملات الإسلامية .

كما حظي سماحة الشيخ باستقبال خاص من معالي الأستاذ الدكتور أحمد محمد علي مدير البنك الإسلامي للتنمية وكبار معاونيه في مكتبه قبل المحاضرة .
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh al-Dedew lectures at the Research and Studies Centre of the Islamic Development Bank in Jeddah.

His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, delivered a lecture at the Research and Studies Centre of the Islamic Development Bank in Jeddah today, Monday (15/09/1432 AH), corresponding to (15/09/2011 CE), under the title: The foundations of transactions (muʿāmalāt) in the Islamic Sharia. In it he took up:

• The nature of the Sharia in setting out rulings, comparing it with man-made law, and showing that the Sharia states rulings with their operative causes (ʿilal) and grounds given, whereas the man-made laws state them stripped of that.

• The Qur'anic texts that deal with the contract, and the aspects of it that they deal with.

• Contracts [that are] prohibited, and the respects in which they are prohibited, in general terms.

• The conditions (shurūṭ) of contracts, in general terms.

• The respects in which contracts are given latitude and the respects in which they are restricted.

The lecture closed with discussions from those present on a number of the questions the lecture had raised.

The lecture was chaired by Professor Dr al-ʿAyyashi Faddad, the economic expert, and was attended by a large gathering of researchers at the Bank's Centre for Studies and Research and of those concerned with Islamic transactions.

His Eminence the Sheikh was also received privately by His Excellency Professor Dr Ahmad Muhammad ʿAli, director of the Islamic Development Bank, and by his senior aides, in his office before the lecture.

options: reproduce both dates exactly as given and flag the mismatch
flags.note: The two dates do not correspond and neither fits the day named. 15 Ramadan 1432 fell on about 15 August 2011, which was a Monday and matches the record's timestamp; 15 September 2011 was a Thursday. The Gregorian figure appears to be a slip for 15/08/2011, in which the month was carried over from the hijri date. Both are reproduced exactly as the source gives them and neither is corrected, per style guide section 11.

flags.arabic: • العقود المنهي وأوجه النهي عنها إجمالا.
flags.context: third of the five headings the lecture covered
options: render with a visible bracketed completion, as done here
read as العقود المنهي عنها and render without marking
leave the lacuna open with an ellipsis
flags.note: المنهي is left dangling in the Arabic: the phrase requires عنها to be complete (العقود المنهي عنها, 'the contracts that are prohibited'). The word is missing in the source. The English supplies the sense in square brackets so that the reader can see something was missing rather than meeting a silently repaired sentence. Style guide section 11 forbids silent repair.

options: the foundations of transactions (muʿāmalāt) in the Islamic Sharia
the principles of Islamic commercial law
the fundamentals of dealings in Islamic law
flags.note: أصول here is 'foundations' in the sense of the root principles a body of law rests on, not uṣūl al-fiqh as a discipline, and معاملات is the glossary's 'transactions'. Option 2 would be the natural phrase for a banking audience but would narrow معاملات to commerce, which it is wider than.

translator_notes: A news report on a lecture. It gives the lecture's five headings and no content under any of them, so no ruling is stated anywhere in the record and the five-rulings mapping of style guide section 3 is not engaged. In particular, the third heading announces that prohibited contracts were treated but names none of them and gives no ruling word.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the report was written.
